finding.problem: auto_deploy lets the system deploy with no person involved. The existing deploy action says 'Only a person deploys' and has requires: human and records_decision: true. The glossary's deploy floor lists 'a person deploys' as a rule no declaration can weaken. auto_deploy has actor system, no requires: human and no records_decision. It calls the same kernel deploy, so the kernel floor would refuse it every time, or else the floor is weakened. Either way this contradicts the existing rule.
finding.where: delivery/delivery.domain.yaml, actions.auto_deploy vs actions.deploy and glossary 'deploy floor'

findings.label: seeded
findings.why: Identifies that system-actor auto_deploy contradicts the 'only a person deploys' rule (requires: human on deploy and the deploy floor).

finding.problem: auto_deploy passes approver: target.approver. That is the person who approved the commit in Authoring, not someone who chose to deploy. The deployment is recorded under that name although they did not trigger it, which gives a false decision trail. deploy uses actor.id, the person actually deploying.

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: Passing target.approver as the deploy approver records a person who did not trigger the deploy, a genuine false decision-trail issue distinct from the seeded conflict.

finding.problem: The only guard is harness_ok == true, which can be stale. From 'done' (for example R3, harness_ok true), preview moves the request back to 'built' without clearing harness_ok. auto_deploy is then allowed in 'built' before the new build's result is recorded. It would deploy a build whose harness has not run. A person pressing deploy can judge this; an automatic deploy cannot. There is also no guard against redeploying from 'done' when deployed is already true, so it can repeat.
finding.where: delivery/delivery.domain.yaml, actions.auto_deploy.preconditions and transitions DeliveryRequest built/done auto_deploy

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: harness_ok may be stale after preview returns a request from done to built, and auto_deploy is allowed in built and done, so it could deploy an unverified build or redeploy.

finding.problem: Nothing triggers auto_deploy after a passing preview. There is no handoff, no reply or event on record_build, and no wiring in the composition. The system actor never fires it, so the stated goal of deploying without anyone pressing deploy is not met. There is also no scenario covering auto_deploy.

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: Nothing triggers auto_deploy after record_build, so the request's intent of deploying automatically after a passing preview is not wired, a real gap.

finding.problem: Other text that describes how deploys work was not updated. The glossary's 'deploy floor' still says a person deploys. The deploy description says 'Only a person deploys'. The scenarios cover only the manual path. These now disagree with the existence of an automatic path.

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: Glossary, deploy description, and scenarios still state a person deploys and cover only the manual path, now inconsistent with auto_deploy; this follows from the seeded conflict but is a real stale-documentation issue.

edit.why: It adds an auto_deploy system action with a preview-passed guard and transitions, but nothing triggers it after record_build's passing preview, so deployment doesn't actually happen on its own.
